newsitem.title: SYRIA: Russia's Primakov holds Mideast talks in Syria.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Primakov holds Mideast talks in Syria.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov held talks with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad in Damascus on Tuesday on how to revive the stalled Middle East peace process.
Presidential spokesman Joubran Kourieh said Primakov, on a regional tour to obtain a greator role for Moscow in the peace process, expressed his "satisfaction" over his talks in Syria.
Primakov arrived in Damascus on Monday at the start of a tour which will take him also to Lebanon, Jordan, Egypt, Israel and the Palestinian self-ruled areas.
He had talks on Monday night with Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara who was also present at the meeting with Assad.

Primakov told reporters on arrival in Syria that Moscow, a co-sponsor of the negotiations with the United States, wanted a more active role in the talks which were launched in Madrid in 1991 with Washington as the dominant mediating power.
Syria has held sporadic peace talks with Israel but no negotiations were held since the May election of Benjamin Netanyahu as Israel's prime minister.
Syria and Arab states condemned Netanyahu for refusing to trade occupied Arab lands with peace, a principle which was adopted by the previous Israeli Labour-led government.
Syria wants Israel to announce readiness to withdraw full from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967, before it agrees to resume the negotiations.
